answer: Each agent binds its signing key to one hardware-attested root listed in a public atlas of devices. Registration locks an onyx bond sized to a multiple of the median epoch reward; the same root cannot sponsor a second key. Live remote attestation is required every epoch, and a failed or reused root is slashed. New keys also enter an oasis queue that releases at most a fixed number of identities per block, so issuance cannot be burst-mined. A sybil farm must buy hardware, lock a new bond, and wait in the queue for every extra identity; copied software keys share one root and earn nothing.
